issues.legal_issue: Restoration of an execution proceeding dismissed for default revives an attachment for the period before dismissal, so private transfers made while the attachment was in force remain ineffective against claims enforceable under it.
material_facts: A decree-holder initiated execution proceedings, and property belonging to the judgment-debtor was attached.
The judgment-debtor and a subsequent purchaser transferred portions of the property while the attachment was in force and before the execution proceeding was dismissed for default.
The execution proceeding was later restored, and the purchasers sought release of the property from attachment.
issues.conclusion: Restoration revived the attachment for the period during which it had been in force before dismissal. Because the transfers occurred during that period, they were void against claims enforceable under the attachment. The appeal was allowed and the order dismissing the purchasers’ release application was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Section 64 of the Code of Civil Procedure makes a private transfer of attached property void against claims enforceable under the attachment. Order 21 Rule 57, as amended by the Calcutta High Court, provides that attachment ceases upon dismissal for default unless the court orders otherwise. Applying the principle in Tavvala Veeraswami v. Pulim Ramanna that restoration revives ancillary orders, including attachment, the Court held that restoration revives the attachment for the period before dismissal. It referred also to Sushila Bala Dasi v. Guest Keen Williams Ltd., Annapurna Patrani v. Lakshmana Kara, and Pradyut Natwarlal Shah v. Suryakant H. Sangani; it distinguished Patringa Koer v. Madhavanand Ram because the transfers there at issue were made during the interval after dismissal, whereas the transfers here preceded dismissal. The Court did not decide the effect of restoration on transfers made during that interval.

predicates.execution_proceeding_dismissed_for_defau: An execution proceeding was dismissed because of a default.
predicates.execution_proceeding_restored: The dismissed execution proceeding was later restored.
predicates.private_transfer_made_while_attachment_s: A private transfer of the property was made while an attachment over it was in force and before the execution proceeding was dismissed.

issues.definition: When an execution proceeding dismissed for default is restored and a private transfer was made while the attachment was in force before dismissal, that transfer remains void against claims enforceable under the attachment.
